statement: A curve is given by $x=t^{2}$, $y=t^{3}$. Find $\\tfrac{dy}{dx}$, and show that the tangent at $t=2$ meets the curve again at the point $(-1,-1)$.
solution: $\\tfrac{dx}{dt}=2t$, $\\tfrac{dy}{dt}=3t^{2}$, so $\\tfrac{dy}{dx}=\\tfrac{3t}{2}$. At $t=2$: $(x,y)=(4,8)$, gradient $3$; tangent $y-8=3(x-4)$, i.e. $y=3x-4$. On the curve $y=t^{3}$, $x=t^{2}$: $t^{3}=3t^{2}-4\\Rightarrow t^{3}-3t^{2}+4=0=(t-2)^{2}(t+1)$. The roots are $t=2$ (contact) and $t=-1$, giving the second point $(-1,-1)$.
hints: Substitute the parametric form into the tangent line.
